summary: Lisa Grumbach works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She held a post at Stanford University (attested 1996) and served as an assistant professor (助教授) at the Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Lisa N. Owen is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Texas at Austin under doctoral supervisor Janice Leoshko, and studied under Walter M. Spink in 1995.

Lita Peipina is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned an MA at the University of Oslo (attested 2008) under MA supervisor Jens Braarvig in 2003, and also studied under Jens-Uwe Hartmann.

Liu Zaifu (1941–2026) was a Sinologist who studied at Xiamen University (~1959–1963). He held posts at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (1963) and the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (~1999), and taught Jinhua Jia.

Lloyd W. Pflueger is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He earned his doctorate at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and served as Professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University (attested 2015).

Lobsang Dargyay (1935–1994) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rahor Monastery, Drepung Monastery (~1952–1959), and earned a Dr.phil. at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1970–1974), later teaching Donald Hamilton.

Lobsang Gyatso (1928–1997) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who studied at Drepung Monastery (~1940–1959). He headed the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics (~1973–1997) and taught Georges Dreyfus, Jay L. Garfield, and Guy Newland, among others.

Lobsang Jamspal (born 1936) specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1964–1971) and Columbia University under Alex Wayman (~1975–1991), holding posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, University of Delhi, and Columbia.
Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa (1926–2008) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Dudjom Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and taught John W. Pettit.

Lobsang Shastri specializes in Tibetology. He served as Head Librarian of the Tibetan Section at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (attested 2003–2006) and as Senior Librarian at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (attested 2018).

Lobsang Tenpa works in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history and archaeology. He earned a Master of Philosophy at Jawaharlal Nehru University, where he studied under supervisor Sharad Kumar Soni.

Lobsang Yongdan works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He studied at Kumbum Monastery and completed a PhD at the University of Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger (ending 2014), later holding postdoctoral posts at Bonn and the Max Planck Institute.

Loden Sherab Dagyab (born 1940) is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Tenzin Gyatso, the 14th Dalai Lama (~1959), and held an academic post at the University of Bonn (~1966–2004).

Lodrö Sangpo (born 1953) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Ernst Steinkellner. He founded the Nitartha Institute in 1996 and served as a senior teacher at Gampo Abbey (attested 2008).

Lokesh Chandra (born 1927) is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar. He studied under Raghu Vira, at University of the Punjab, and completed a PhD at Utrecht University (~1949–1950), serving as Secretary and Director at the International Academy of Indian Culture.
Longlian (1909–2006) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Tibetology. She studied under Fazun in 1939 and under Nenghai as her traditional teacher from ~1941 to 1967.

Lopon Tenzin Namdak (1927–2025) studied at Menri Monastery and under Sangye Tenzin and Gangru Tsultrim Gyaltsen. A specialist in Tibetology and religious studies, he founded Menri and Triten Norbutse monasteries, serving as Lopon at both.

Lore Sander (1936–2023) specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, having studied under Ernst Waldschmidt. She served as Curator at the Museum für Asiatische Kunst and held posts at Humboldt, Munich, and Free University of Berlin.

Lori Meeks (born 1976) specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She completed doctoral studies under Jacqueline I. Stone and Ryuichi Abe, held a postdoctoral fellowship at Stanford (~2003–2004), and became Assistant Professor at USC in ~2004.

Lorna Dewaraja (1929–2014) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She held posts at St Anne's College and at the University of Ceylon, where she was Associate Professor of History.
